question: What incentive values does the SuSI Program's ADI offer for net metered non-residential projects located on rooftops, carports, canopies, and floating solar in New Jersey?
gold_answers: The ADI Program offers $110 per SREC-II for net metered non-residential projects smaller than 1 MW and $100 per SREC-II for projects between 1 MW and 5 MW. Public entities can receive an additional $20 adder, making it $130 per SREC-II for smaller projects and $120 per SREC-II for larger ones.

question: As a commercial subscriber in Louisiana, what information is my Subscriber Organization legally obligated to maintain on file with CURO regarding the CSG Facility they operate in New Orleans?
gold_answers: Subscriber Organizations must maintain the owner’s name and address, business address, name of registered agent in Orleans Parish, general information on the facility including location, DC and AC nameplate capacity, major equipment list, interconnection requirements, proof of liability insurance, proof of registration with the Louisiana Secretary of State, and proof of professional licenses from applicable regulatory agencies.

selected.text: Pursuant to Section III.K.

selected.text: The Year 1 Decision finalized the Year 1 Program Manual and set NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2022.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Decision finalized the Year 2 Program Manual, established NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2023, and authorized several changes to the Program’s application requirements to better align the Program with the Program Objectives.

question: What does the City of Sacramento require for newly constructed buildings in terms of all-electric building requirements?
gold_answers:
All newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings if permit applications are filed on or after January 1, 2023.
**Context** - For building permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023, except as provided in subsections 101.12.6 and 101.12.7, all newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings.

### QA Pair 2
**Question** - When does the requirement for all newly constructed buildings to be all-electric become mandatory in Sacramento?
**Answer** - The requirement becomes mandatory for buildings with permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023.
**Context** - For building permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023, except as provided in subsections 101.12.6 and 101.12.7, all newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings.

### QA Pair 3
**Question** - What exemptions are available for constructing mixed fuel buildings under the City of Sacramento's policy?
**Answer** - Limited exemptions include ground floor food service establishments for areas with cooking equipment, manufacturing or industrial facilities with process loads, and water-heating systems in regulated affordable housing where virtual net energy metering is unavailable.
**Context** - Limited exemptions for building permit applications filed on or before December 31, 2025, include ground floor food service establishments, manufacturing or industrial facilities, and regulated affordable housing.

### QA Pair 4
**Question** - When does the exemption for limited sectors end in relation to the all-electric building requirements in Sacramento?
**Answer** - The exemptions for limited sectors such as ground floor food service establishments, manufacturing or industrial facilities, and regulated affordable housing end on January 1, 2026.
**Context** - The section 101.12.1 and section 101.12.2 requirements to construct all-electric buildings shall not apply to sectors with limited exemptions until January 1, 2026

selected.text: # General Information As part of your local Municipal Utility's commitment to maintaining low cost, reliable electric service, your local Municipal Utility is pleased to offer the Connected Homes Program ("Program").

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: As a member of the Massachusetts Municipal Wholesale Electric Company ("MMWEC"), your local Municipal Utility is able to participate in the Program, which is administered through MMWEC's NextZero program to allow active management of Wi-Fi enabled residential devices for customers wishing to participate in a residential demand reduction program.

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: The Program is being offered to your local Municipal Utility's customers as part of MMWEC's suite of energy efficiency opportunities administered through NextZero.

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: MMWEC is the authorized agent of your local Municipal Utility with respect to the Program.

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: The Program uses a cloud-based platform provided by Virtual Peaker, Inc. ("Virtual Peaker") to exercise load control and deliver capacity and RNS savings.

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: The Program offers credits to customers in exchange for temporarily allowing the utility the ability to adjust thermostats, hot water heaters, EV chargers, home batteries, and other eligible devices in the customer's home to help minimize energy usage at peak times of the month.

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: Peak energy usage (typically occurring between 5:00-9:00 p.m.) can account for more than $40\%$ of Massachusetts electric customer's annual electricity costs.

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: Customers enrolling one or more devices in the Program and opting to participate during a peak day will be given credits against their utility bills $[\wedge_{\mathbf{1}}]$ .

selected.title: 1. OVERVIEW
selected.text: OVERVIEW The purpose of the Community Solar Rules ("Rules") is to establish the City Council of New Orleans′ rules, policies, and procedures for Community Solar Generating ("CSG") Facilities and the associated electric utility customer subscriptions in Orleans Parish, including: eligibility for participating in Community Solar Generating Facilities; developer, facility, and customer limits with respect to cormmunity solar; establishment of a bill crediting mechanism for participants; customer protection provisions; general interconnection requirements; safety and performance requirements; and contractual and reporting requirements.

selected.title: 1. OVERVIEW
selected.text: Further, these rules are intended to establish a clear and streamlined path to the development of Community Solar development in the City of New Orleans.

selected.title: 1. OVERVIEW
selected.text: The Council recognizes that these rules do not provide the only path to distributed generation development in the City of New Orleans.

selected.title: 1. OVERVIEW
selected.text: To the extent that the Utility or any other party has a proposed project or proposal that does not adhere to the requirements of these Rules, it may submit a proposal to the Council for review and approval.

selected.title: 1. OVERVIEW
selected.text: These Rules shall be cited as the “New Orleans Community Solar Rules."

selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: No LMI Incentive will be available beyond the end of 2027.

selected.text: The Company has discretion to allocate the LMI Incentive budget so that applications and disbursements under this program may be taken and paid throughout the calendar year.

selected.text: A Customer shall receive the applicable LMI Incentive amount as a check via U.S. Mail (or electronic payment) following the Company’s inspection and approval of the installation of the Renewable Energy DGF and verification of eligibility.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: # B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING On June 30, 2021, the Authority established a combined successor program to the state’s Low and Zero Emissions Renewable Energy Credit (LREC/ZREC) and Virtual Net Metering (VNM) programs for non-residential customers, termed the NRES Program.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: Decision, June 30, 2021, Docket No. 20-07-01, PURA Implementation of Section 3 of Public Act 19-35, Renewable Energy Tariffs and Procurement Plans (Non-Residential Tariff Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: Pursuant to Section III.K.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: of the Non-Residential Tariff Decision, the Authority initiates an annual docket to review key Program metrics with stakeholders and to evaluate whether and how the Program should be modified to more fully accomplish the objectives established in the Non-Residential Tariff Decision.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: This proceeding serves as the administrative record for the Authority’s review and approval of the Year 3 NRES Program Manual and other key compliance filings.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the first annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 21- 08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Tariff Program Review – Year 1, issuing a Decision on November 3, 2021 (Year 1 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Year 1 Decision finalized the Year 1 Program Manual and set NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2022.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the second annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 22-08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions Program Review – Year 2, issuing a Decision on November 9, 2022 (Year 2 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Decision finalized the Year 2 Program Manual, established NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2023, and authorized several changes to the Program’s application requirements to better align the Program with the Program Objectives.

selected.text: The gap between the upper bound of “low-income” and the lower bound of “moderateincome” was accidental, and has been corrected, by changing “moderateincome household” to be income in excess of $\mathbf{\pi}^{\leftarrow}200$ percent of the Federal poverty line...,” rather than “50 percent ... of the median income.”

selected.title: policy 22434
selected.text: The BPU notes that the standards used in these two definitions are in line with those used in other New Jersey State programs.

selected.title: policy 22434
selected.text: 42. COMMENT: While the commented does not necessarily oppose the definitions of “low-income household” and “moderate-income household,” it does question whether race was sufficiently considered before these definitions were adopted.

selected.title: policy 22434
selected.text: The commenter believes that race should be considered in some manner when fashioning a definition for low- and moderate-income.

selected.title: policy 22434
selected.text: The rules also do not indicate how many residents would fall under the proposed definition and how many of those would be people of color.

selected.title: policy 22434
selected.text: The BPU should make this information known, so interested stakeholders can make informed comments on this very important topic.

selected.title: policy 22434
selected.text: Another commenter supports the suggestion to conduct a racial sensitivity analysis, to determine how many people of color may fit within the definitions in the Proposed Rule relating to low-income and moderate-income households.

selected.text: # General Information As part of your local Municipal Utility's commitment to maintaining low cost, reliable electric service, your local Municipal Utility is pleased to offer the Connected Homes Program ("Program").

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: As a member of the Massachusetts Municipal Wholesale Electric Company ("MMWEC"), your local Municipal Utility is able to participate in the Program, which is administered through MMWEC's NextZero program to allow active management of Wi-Fi enabled residential devices for customers wishing to participate in a residential demand reduction program.

selected.text: The Program is being offered to your local Municipal Utility's customers as part of MMWEC's suite of energy efficiency opportunities administered through NextZero.

selected.title: General Information
selected.text: MMWEC is the authorized agent of your local Municipal Utility with respect to the Program.

selected.text: The Program offers credits to customers in exchange for temporarily allowing the utility the ability to adjust thermostats, hot water heaters, EV chargers, home batteries, and other eligible devices in the customer's home to help minimize energy usage at peak times of the month.

selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: No LMI Incentive will be available beyond the end of 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The Company has discretion to allocate the LMI Incentive budget so that applications and disbursements under this program may be taken and paid throughout the calendar year.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: A Customer shall receive the applicable LMI Incentive amount as a check via U.S. Mail (or electronic payment) following the Company’s inspection and approval of the installation of the Renewable Energy DGF and verification of eligibility.

the third proviso of this paragraph in this Act the Secretary shall distribute the remaining funds made available under this paragraph in this Act among States as follows— (A) 75 percent by the proportion that the total cost of replacing all bridges classified in poor condition in such State bears to the sum of the total cost to replace all bridges classified in poor condition in all States; and (B) 25 percent by the proportion that the total cost of rehabilitating all bridges classified in fair condition in such State bears to the sum of the total cost to rehabilitate all bridges classified in fair condition in all States: Provided further, That the amounts calculated under the preceding proviso shall be adjusted such that each State receives, for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026, no less than $\$45,000,000$ under such proviso: Provided further, That for purposes of the preceding 2 provisos, the Secretary shall determine replacement and rehabilitation costs based on the average unit costs of bridges from 2016 through 2020, as submitted by States to the Federal Highway Administration, as required by section 144(b)(5) of title 23, United States Code: Provided further, That for purposes of determining the distribution of funds to States under this paragraph in this Act, the Secretary shall calculate the total deck area of bridges classified as in poor or fair condition based on the National Bridge Inventory as of December 31, 2020: Provided further, That, subject to the following proviso, funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to States shall be used for highway bridge replacement, rehabilitation, preservation, protec tion, or construction projects on public roads: Provided further, That of the funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to a State, 15 percent shall be set aside for use on off-system bridges for the same purposes as described in the preceding proviso: Provided further, That, except as provided in the following proviso, for funds made available under this para graph in this Act that are distributed to States, the Federal share shall be determined in accordance with section 120 of title 23, United States Code: Provided further, That for funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to States and used on an off-system bridge that is owned by a county, town, township, city, municipality or other local agency, or federally recognized Tribe the Federal share shall be 100 percent; (2) $\$5,000,000,000$ , to remain available until expended for amounts made available for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026, shall be to carry out a National Electric Vehicle Formula Program (referred to in this paragraph in this Act as the ‘‘Program’’) to provide funding to States to strategically deploy electric vehicle charging infrastructure and to establish an interconnected network to facilitate data collection, access, and reliability: Provided, That funds made available under this paragraph in this Act shall be used for: (1) the acquisition and installation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure to serve as a catalyst for the deployment of such infrastructure and to connect it to a network to facilitate data collection, access, and reliability; (2) proper operation and maintenance of electric vehicle charging infrastructure; and (3) data sharing Determination.

question: As a commercial business owner in Iowa, how does the Energy Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program evaluate projects for approval, and what specific criteria must be met to be considered for a loan exceeding $1 million?
gold_answers: The program evaluates projects based on whether they demonstrate broad reaching benefits to the state, local community, or utility ratepayers, a creative or innovative approach to a need or problem, or if assistance is necessary to reduce the project's risks. Applicants requesting a loan over $1 million must, at a minimum, demonstrate that the project offers broad reaching benefits.

question: As a farmer in California, what is my legal obligation when installing a variable speed drive (VSD) for an agricultural process fan to be eligible for the PG&E GoGreen Business Energy Financing rebate?
gold_answers: To install an Agricultural Process Fan VSD, the fan must not be used for HVAC, exhaust, pressurization or other process applications. The individual fan motors must not exceed 5 horsepower (hp), and the fan must operate continuously or be manually operated with an ON/OFF control switch. Additionally, the fan motors must not be two-speed or have an existing VSD, and the VSD must control multiple fans up to 5 hp each in arrays with one VSD or with one VSD for each fan. The VSD must vary the speed of the fan automatically based on ambient conditions, and the rebate is applicable only to agricultural buildings in certain climate zones (CZ06, CZ07, CZ08, CZ09, CZ10, CZ11, CZ12, CZ13, CZ14, and CZ15).

selected.text: Pursuant to Section III.K.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: This proceeding serves as the administrative record for the Authority’s review and approval of the Year 3 NRES Program Manual and other key compliance filings.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the first annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 21- 08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Tariff Program Review – Year 1, issuing a Decision on November 3, 2021 (Year 1 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Year 1 Decision finalized the Year 1 Program Manual and set NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2022.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the second annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 22-08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions Program Review – Year 2, issuing a Decision on November 9, 2022 (Year 2 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Decision finalized the Year 2 Program Manual, established NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2023, and authorized several changes to the Program’s application requirements to better align the Program with the Program Objectives.

selected.text: Customers to whom this Schedule NEM-2 is applicable pursuant to Section II.A may be eligible for the Low-to-Moderate Income Benefits Adder upon certification that (1) the Customer’s total annual combined gross household income does not exceed $225\%$ of the federal poverty level, (2) the electric service account for which the Low-to-Moderate Income Benefits Adder is requested is located at the Customer’s primary residence, and (3) the Customer has not and will not request the Low-to-Moderate Income Benefits Adder for any electric service account other than the customer’s primary residence.

selected.text: Certification of eligibility shall be subject to audit and verification as deemed necessary by Entergy Mississippi.

question: What is the Residential Demand Response Battery Incentive Program in Entergy Mississippi, and what are its key requirements?
gold_answers: The Residential Demand Response Battery Incentive Program is a policy from Entergy Mississippi that offers a one-time $2,000 cash incentive to any retail residential customer with an eligible DGIC (distributed generation interconnection customer) who installs a battery storage system with a minimum storage capacity of 8 kWh and enrolls in the Company's Battery Demand Response program. The customer must certify that the battery complies with the company's Battery Demand Response Program. This incentive is available on a first-come, first-served basis until the end of 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: No LMI Incentive will be available beyond the end of 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The Company has discretion to allocate the LMI Incentive budget so that applications and disbursements under this program may be taken and paid throughout the calendar year.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: A Customer shall receive the applicable LMI Incentive amount as a check via U.S. Mail (or electronic payment) following the Company’s inspection and approval of the installation of the Renewable Energy DGF and verification of eligibility.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In lieu of receiving the LMI Incentive directly, a Customer may assign the LMI Incentive to a solar installer, contractor, or vendor by making such an election in the Customer’s Interconnection Application submitted to the Company.

selected.text: Customers to whom this Schedule NEM-2 is applicable pursuant to Section II.A may be eligible for the Low-to-Moderate Income Benefits Adder upon certification that (1) the Customer’s total annual combined gross household income does not exceed $225\%$ of the federal poverty level, (2) the electric service account for which the Low-to-Moderate Income Benefits Adder is requested is located at the Customer’s primary residence, and (3) the Customer has not and will not request the Low-to-Moderate Income Benefits Adder for any electric service account other than the customer’s primary residence.

selected.title: III. NET MONTHLY BILL
selected.text: Certification of eligibility shall be subject to audit and verification as deemed necessary by Entergy Mississippi.

selected.text: The Low-to-Moderate Income Benefits Adder shall apply to all residential Customers who meet these qualifications and who are approved to take service under this Schedule, and for such qualifying Customers shall remain in place for 25 years from the date the Customer begins taking net metering service under the Schedule, subject to audit and verification by Entergy Mississippi of the Customer’s eligibility.

question: What are the conditions for residential customers to be eligible for Madison Gas & Electric's Charge Ahead Program?

selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

and (B) 25 percent by the proportion that the total cost of rehabilitating all bridges classified in fair condition in such State bears to the sum of the total cost to rehabilitate all bridges classified in fair condition in all States: Provided further, That the amounts calculated under the preceding proviso shall be adjusted such that each State receives, for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026, no less than $\$45,000,000$ under such proviso: Provided further, That for purposes of the preceding 2 provisos, the Secretary shall determine replacement and rehabilitation costs based on the average unit costs of bridges from 2016 through 2020, as submitted by States to the Federal Highway Administration, as required by section 144(b)(5) of title 23, United States Code: Provided further, That for purposes of determining the distribution of funds to States under this paragraph in this Act, the Secretary shall calculate the total deck area of bridges classified as in poor or fair condition based on the National Bridge Inventory as of December 31, 2020: Provided further, That, subject to the following proviso, funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to States shall be used for highway bridge replacement, rehabilitation, preservation, protec tion, or construction projects on public roads: Provided further, That of the funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to a State, 15 percent shall be set aside for use on off-system bridges for the same purposes as described in the preceding proviso: Provided further, That, except as provided in the following proviso, for funds made available under this para graph in this Act that are distributed to States, the Federal share shall be determined in accordance with section 120 of title 23, United States Code: Provided further, That for funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to States and used on an off-system bridge that is owned by a county, town, township, city, municipality or other local agency, or federally recognized Tribe the Federal share shall be 100 percent; (2) $\$5,000,000,000$ , to remain available until expended for amounts made available for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026, shall be to carry out a National Electric Vehicle Formula Program (referred to in this paragraph in this Act as the ‘‘Program’’) to provide funding to States to strategically deploy electric vehicle charging infrastructure and to establish an interconnected network to facilitate data collection, access, and reliability: Provided, That funds made available under this paragraph in this Act shall be used for: (1) the acquisition and installation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure to serve as a catalyst for the deployment of such infrastructure and to connect it to a network to facilitate data collection, access, and reliability; (2) proper operation and maintenance of electric vehicle charging infrastructure; and (3) data sharing Determination.

selected.text: # B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING On June 30, 2021, the Authority established a combined successor program to the state’s Low and Zero Emissions Renewable Energy Credit (LREC/ZREC) and Virtual Net Metering (VNM) programs for non-residential customers, termed the NRES Program.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: Pursuant to Section III.K.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: of the Non-Residential Tariff Decision, the Authority initiates an annual docket to review key Program metrics with stakeholders and to evaluate whether and how the Program should be modified to more fully accomplish the objectives established in the Non-Residential Tariff Decision.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: This proceeding serves as the administrative record for the Authority’s review and approval of the Year 3 NRES Program Manual and other key compliance filings.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the first annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 21- 08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Tariff Program Review – Year 1, issuing a Decision on November 3, 2021 (Year 1 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Year 1 Decision finalized the Year 1 Program Manual and set NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2022.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the second annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 22-08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions Program Review – Year 2, issuing a Decision on November 9, 2022 (Year 2 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Decision finalized the Year 2 Program Manual, established NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2023, and authorized several changes to the Program’s application requirements to better align the Program with the Program Objectives.

question: What are the requirements for a Community Solar Generating (CSG) Facility to be eligible in New Orleans, Louisiana?
gold_answers: A CSG Facility can be owned by any for-profit or nonprofit entity or organization. It must be located in the Utility's service territory, individually metered, and connected to the Utility's distribution system. The Subscriber Organization must enter into a Contract with the Utility to sell the Output from the facility to the Utility, taking the form of a credit against the Subscriber's electric bill.

question: What is the method for determining the fair cash value of commercial solar energy system improvements in counties with fewer than 3,000,000 inhabitants under the Improvement Valuation of Commercial Solar Energy Systems policy?
gold_answers:
The fair cash value is determined by subtracting the allowance for physical depreciation from the trended real property cost basis.
**Context** - (35 ILCS 200/10-725 new)  
Sec. 10-725. Improvement valuation of commercial solar energy systems in counties with fewer than 3,000,000 inhabitants. Beginning in assessment year 2018, the fair cash value of commercial solar energy system improvements in counties with fewer than 3,000,000 inhabitants shall be determined by subtracting the allowance for physical depreciation from the trended real property cost basis.

### QA Pair number 2
**Question** - Are commercial solar energy systems assessable under this Division subject to equalization factors applied by the Department or any board of review, assessor, or chief county assessment officer?
**Answer** - No.
**Context** - (35 ILCS 200/10-735 new) Sec. 10-735. Commercial solar energy systems not subject to equalization. Commercial solar energy systems assessable under this Division are not subject to equalization factors applied by the Department or any board of review, assessor, or chief county assessment officer.

### QA Pair number 3
**Question** - What does the owner of a ground installed commercial solar energy system need to do upon commissioning a metes and bounds survey description of the land?
**Answer** - The owner shall deliver a copy of the survey to the chief county assessment officer and to the owner of the land upon which the ground installed commercial solar energy system is constructed.
**Context** - (35 ILCS 200/10-740 new)  
Sec. 10-740. Survey for ground installed commercial solar energy systems; parcel identification numbers for property improved with a ground installed commercial solar energy system. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the owner of the ground installed commercial solar energy system shall commission a metes and bounds survey description of the land upon which the commercial solar energy system is installed, including access routes, over which the owner of the commercial solar energy system has exclusive control.

### QA Pair number 4
**Question** - Who is liable for real estate taxes for the land and real property improvements of a ground-installed commercial solar energy system?
**Answer** - The owner of the commercial solar energy system is liable.
**Context** - # (35 ILCS 200/10-745 new)  
Sec. 10-745. Real estate taxes. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 9-175 of this Code, the owner of the commercial solar energy system shall be liable for the real estate taxes for the land and real property improvements of a ground installed commercial solar energy system

question: As a low-income residential customer participating in Entergy Mississippi's Residential Demand Response Battery Incentive Program with a Distributed Generation Facility (DGF), how is my bill calculated, and what happens to my excess energy credits?
gold_answers: Your monthly bill will be the total of any charges for usage as recorded on meter Channel 1, minus any credit due to you from excess energy exported to the Company as recorded on meter Channel 2. However, your excess energy credits will not be applied to reduce any fixed monthly customer charges or minimum bill provisions. Any remaining excess energy bill credit at the end of your service period will be issued to you as a check.

question: As a distributor in Nevada, what are the requirements to be considered under the Nevada Appliance and Equipment Energy Efficiency Standards?

question: What additional eligibility requirements must a customer satisfy to qualify for increased incentives under the Equitable Solar Initiative?
gold_answers: The customer must be owned and operated by one of the nine federally recognized tribes of Oregon, an affordable multifamily property where at least 50% of the units are dedicated to residents below 80% AMI, an eligible nonprofit organization with a mission to benefit underrepresented communities, or an Eligible Nonprofit Organization.

selected.title: 6.1.1 Trade Ally Eligibility and Expectations
selected.text: In addition to standard customer service expectations, Energy Trust requires all participating Solar Electric Trade Allies offering increased incentives as part of the Equitable Solar Initiative to comply with the following additional customer service standards: Trade Ally must respond to Energy Trust or customer requests in a timely manner and resolve application revisions and installation corrections within required timelines.

selected.title: 6.1.1 Trade Ally Eligibility and Expectations
selected.text: # 6.2 Residential Incentives # 6.2.1 Solar Within Reach Overview House Bill 3141, the public-purpose charge modernization bill passed by the Oregon legislature in 2021, requires that $25\%$ of the funding allocated to Energy Trust’s renewable energy programs benefits customers with low and moderate incomes.

selected.title: 6.2.2 Solar Within Reach Trade Ally Participation Requirements
selected.text: All other Energy Trust eligibility requirements for residential incentive program participation continue to apply.

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: # 6.3.1 Overview Helping the entities that serve and support lower-income customers, communities of color, and rural communities is an important way to overcome awareness barriers and foster access.

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: As part of the Equitable Solar Initiative, Energy Trust offers increased incentives for eligible customers as a way of combatting some of the additional financial and market barriers to installing solar.

selected.title: 6.1.1 Trade Ally Eligibility and Expectations
selected.text: # 6.1.1 Trade Ally Eligibility and Expectations Except where otherwise noted, all Solar Electric Trade Allies are eligible to offer increased incentives as part of the Equitable Solar Initiative.

selected.title: 6.2.2 Solar Within Reach Trade Ally Participation Requirements
selected.text: Only income-qualified customers are eligible to receive Solar Within Reach incentives.

selected.title: 6.2.2 Solar Within Reach Trade Ally Participation Requirements
selected.text: Before an incentive can be reserved, a signed copy of the customer’s Solar Within Reach Income Verification (Form 210SWR) OR Solar Within Reach for Builders Qualification Verification (Form 210B) must be submitted to Energy Trust, along with all other required incentive application documentation, as a part of the standard application process in PowerClerk.

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: Tribal: Owned and operated by one of the nine federally recognized tribes of Oregon Affordable Multifamily Property: An affordable multifamily property where at least $50\%$ of the property’s dwelling units associated with the project, are and shall remain dedicated for residents who are at or below $80\%$ Area Median Income (AMI) for at least 10 years after project completion Eligible Nonprofit Organization: Owned and operated by a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: (i) is registered with the Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division,

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: (ii) is not identified on the Oregon Department of Justice list of “Disqualified Charities,” and

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: (iii) has a stated mission and track record of delivering programs directly benefiting communities and individuals including, but not limited to, Black, Indigenous, and other communities of color, communities experiencing lower incomes, federally recognized Indian tribes, rural communities, coastal communities, communities with limited infrastructure, and other communities and individuals traditionally underrepresented in public processes and programs to incent and advance solar energy installations Other eligibility requirements for program participation include: o Electric utility must be Portland General Electric or Pacific Power o Maximum project size: <360 kW-AC (about 480 kW-DC) o Project cannot have an existing incentive reservation with Energy Trust o Installation site may be existing or new construction o Maximum incentive provided by Energy Trust shall not exceed $75\%$ of the eligible Total Project Cost # 6.3.3 Incentive Allocations and Availability Nonresidential, Institutional and Multifamily Equitable Solar Initiative incentives are available on a first-come first-served basis and are subject to change and availability.

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: Incentive rates will follow standard program procedures and will gradually reduce over time, however, due to Energy Trust’s limited budget, these increased Equitable Solar Initiative incentives may not remain available year-round.

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: Energy Trust will announce all available incentive allocations, rates, and project caps for increased incentives at the beginning of each calendar year.

selected.title: 6.3.1 Overview
selected.text: Energy Trust will not maintain a waitlist.

selected.title: 6.1.1 Trade Ally Eligibility and Expectations
selected.text: In addition to adhering to all requirements set forth in Part 2 of the Program Guide for Solar Electric Trade Allies, Trade Allies accessing incentives offered through the Equitable Solar Initiative are expected to model the highest standards as ambassadors of Energy Trust.

selected.title: 6.1.1 Trade Ally Eligibility and Expectations
selected.text: The increased incentive funding supporting the Equitable Solar Initiative has been intentionally allocated from Energy Trust’s budget in support of our organizational DEI goals, and is specifically targeted at expanding access and the benefits of solar to communities that have not previously had access to it.

selected.title: 6.2.2 Solar Within Reach Trade Ally Participation Requirements
selected.text: The Solar Within Reach Trade Ally must itemize the Solar Within Reach incentive on the customer’s invoice and provide it as an upfront discount on the customer’s invoice.

selected.title: 6.2.2 Solar Within Reach Trade Ally Participation Requirements
selected.text: To apply for incentives, follow the standard incentive application instructions outlined in Part 4 of the Program Guide for Solar Electric Trade Allies, and check the box for Solar Within Reach.

selected.title: Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) Program - Administratively Determined Incentive
selected.text: The SuSI Program is made up of two sub-programs: **[Administratively Determined Incentive Program](https://njcleanenergy.com/renewable-energy/programs/susi-program/adi- program)** The ADI Program provides incentives for net metered residential projects, net metered non-residential projects of 5 MW or less, all community solar projects, and, for an interim period, projects previously eligible to seek conditional certification from the Board under Subsection (t).

selected.title: 6.1.1 Trade Ally Eligibility and Expectations
selected.text: Energy Trust may suspend eligibility to participate in accessing increased incentives, or other offers at any time for failure to abide by program requirements, or for any other reason in its sole discretion by providing written notice to the Trade Ally.

selected.title: 6.2.2 Solar Within Reach Trade Ally Participation Requirements
selected.text: Builders and New Residential Construction Prior to performing any Solar Within Reach work or assessments, the approved Solar Within Reach Trade Ally must confirm with the Builder representative the income eligibility of the end customer and future homeowner of the new residential construction using the Solar Within Reach for Builders Qualification Verification (Form 210B).

question: What support does the Accelerating Clean Transportation (ACT) School Bus Fleet Deployment program offer to school districts facing barriers in electrifying their school bus fleets?
gold_answers: The ACT School Bus Fleet Deployment program offers school bus fleets flexible funding for depot upgrades and purchases of electric school buses and associated charging infrastructure. It also provides an opportunity for participating fleets to work with MassCEC's consultant team to address the gaps in technical knowledge impeding school bus fleets from electrifying, in areas such as coordination with stakeholders, equipment selection, procurement, and project implementation.

selected.text: # B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING On June 30, 2021, the Authority established a combined successor program to the state’s Low and Zero Emissions Renewable Energy Credit (LREC/ZREC) and Virtual Net Metering (VNM) programs for non-residential customers, termed the NRES Program.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: Pursuant to Section III.K.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: of the Non-Residential Tariff Decision, the Authority initiates an annual docket to review key Program metrics with stakeholders and to evaluate whether and how the Program should be modified to more fully accomplish the objectives established in the Non-Residential Tariff Decision.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: This proceeding serves as the administrative record for the Authority’s review and approval of the Year 3 NRES Program Manual and other key compliance filings.

selected.text: The Authority conducted the first annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 21- 08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Tariff Program Review – Year 1, issuing a Decision on November 3, 2021 (Year 1 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Year 1 Decision finalized the Year 1 Program Manual and set NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2022.

selected.text: The Authority conducted the second annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 22-08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions Program Review – Year 2, issuing a Decision on November 9, 2022 (Year 2 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Decision finalized the Year 2 Program Manual, established NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2023, and authorized several changes to the Program’s application requirements to better align the Program with the Program Objectives.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: No LMI Incentive will be available beyond the end of 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The Company has discretion to allocate the LMI Incentive budget so that applications and disbursements under this program may be taken and paid throughout the calendar year.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: A Customer shall receive the applicable LMI Incentive amount as a check via U.S. Mail (or electronic payment) following the Company’s inspection and approval of the installation of the Renewable Energy DGF and verification of eligibility.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In lieu of receiving the LMI Incentive directly, a Customer may assign the LMI Incentive to a solar installer, contractor, or vendor by making such an election in the Customer’s Interconnection Application submitted to the Company.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: # B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING On June 30, 2021, the Authority established a combined successor program to the state’s Low and Zero Emissions Renewable Energy Credit (LREC/ZREC) and Virtual Net Metering (VNM) programs for non-residential customers, termed the NRES Program.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: Decision, June 30, 2021, Docket No. 20-07-01, PURA Implementation of Section 3 of Public Act 19-35, Renewable Energy Tariffs and Procurement Plans (Non-Residential Tariff Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: Pursuant to Section III.K.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: of the Non-Residential Tariff Decision, the Authority initiates an annual docket to review key Program metrics with stakeholders and to evaluate whether and how the Program should be modified to more fully accomplish the objectives established in the Non-Residential Tariff Decision.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: This proceeding serves as the administrative record for the Authority’s review and approval of the Year 3 NRES Program Manual and other key compliance filings.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the first annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 21- 08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Tariff Program Review – Year 1, issuing a Decision on November 3, 2021 (Year 1 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Year 1 Decision finalized the Year 1 Program Manual and set NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2022.

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Authority conducted the second annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 22-08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions Program Review – Year 2, issuing a Decision on November 9, 2022 (Year 2 Decision).

selected.title: B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING
selected.text: The Decision finalized the Year 2 Program Manual, established NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2023, and authorized several changes to the Program’s application requirements to better align the Program with the Program Objectives.

question: I'm planning to install EV chargers at my commercial site in California under the PG&E - EV Fleet Program. What are the incentive amounts for different charger types, specifically for chargers up to 50 kW, between 50.1 kW - 149.9 kW, and 150 kW and above?
gold_answers: For chargers up to 50 kW, the incentive is 50% of the cost of the EV charger, up to $15,000. For chargers between 50.1 kW - 149.9 kW, the incentive is 50% of the cost of the EV charger, up to $25,000. For chargers 150 kW and above, the incentive is 50% of the cost of the EV charger, up to $42,000.

selected.text: The Illinois Solar for All Program consists of four sub-programs: the **Low- Income Single-Family and Small Multifamily Solar Incentive** (also referred to as "**Residential Solar (Small)** "); the **Low-Income Community Solar Project Initiative** (referred to as "**Community Solar** "); the **Non-Profit and Public Facilities** program; and the **Low-Income****Multifamily Solar Incentive** (referred to as "**Residential Solar (Large)** ").

selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: No LMI Incentive will be available beyond the end of 2027.

selected.text: The Company has discretion to allocate the LMI Incentive budget so that applications and disbursements under this program may be taken and paid throughout the calendar year.

selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: No LMI Incentive will be available beyond the end of 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The Company has discretion to allocate the LMI Incentive budget so that applications and disbursements under this program may be taken and paid throughout the calendar year.

selected.text: A Customer shall receive the applicable LMI Incentive amount as a check via U.S. Mail (or electronic payment) following the Company’s inspection and approval of the installation of the Renewable Energy DGF and verification of eligibility.

question: As a commercial motor vehicle operator in Ohio, can you explain how the Motor Carrier Safety Grants will be allocated over the fiscal years 2022 through 2026, and what specific programs will benefit from this funding?
gold_answers: The Motor Carrier Safety Grants will provide up to $622,500,000, with $124,500,000 available for each fiscal year from 2022 through 2026. Specifically, up to $400,000,000 will be allocated to the motor carrier safety assistance program, up to $80,000,000 to the commercial driver’s license program implementation program, and up to $132,500,000 to the high priority activities program, with an additional $10,000,000 for commercial motor vehicle operators grants.

selected.text: As a member of the Massachusetts Municipal Wholesale Electric Company ("MMWEC"), your local Municipal Utility is able to participate in the Program, which is administered through MMWEC's NextZero program to allow active management of Wi-Fi enabled residential devices for customers wishing to participate in a residential demand reduction program.

question: I am an Investor-Owned Utility in Michigan, and I want to understand how the state defines 'modified net metering' in the context of distributed generation. Can you explain the specifics of this billing method and how it impacts customer charges?
gold_answers: Modified net metering applies the power supply component of the full retail rate to the net of the bidirectional flow of kilowatt hours. Standby charges for customers on an energy rate schedule are equal to the retail distribution charge applied to the imputed customer usage during the billing period, which is calculated as the sum of the metered on-site generation and the net power flow.

classified in fair condition in all States: Provided further, That the amounts calculated under the preceding proviso shall be adjusted such that each State receives, for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026, no less than $\$45,000,000$ under such proviso: Provided further, That for purposes of the preceding 2 provisos, the Secretary shall determine replacement and rehabilitation costs based on the average unit costs of bridges from 2016 through 2020, as submitted by States to the Federal Highway Administration, as required by section 144(b)(5) of title 23, United States Code: Provided further, That for purposes of determining the distribution of funds to States under this paragraph in this Act, the Secretary shall calculate the total deck area of bridges classified as in poor or fair condition based on the National Bridge Inventory as of December 31, 2020: Provided further, That, subject to the following proviso, funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to States shall be used for highway bridge replacement, rehabilitation, preservation, protec tion, or construction projects on public roads: Provided further, That of the funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to a State, 15 percent shall be set aside for use on off-system bridges for the same purposes as described in the preceding proviso: Provided further, That, except as provided in the following proviso, for funds made available under this para graph in this Act that are distributed to States, the Federal share shall be determined in Act as the ‘‘Program’’) to provide funding to States to strategically deploy electric vehicle charging infrastructure and to establish an interconnected network to facilitate data collection, access, and reliability: Provided, That funds made available under this paragraph in this Act shall be used for: (1) the acquisition and installation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure to serve as a charging infrastructure; and (3) data sharing Determination.

question: Can you explain the process outlined in Nevada Appliance and Equipment Energy Efficiency Standards for establishing and enforcing energy efficiency standards for appliances sold within the state?

selected.text: Specifically, one commenter believes that a retail rate bill credit will be insufficient to support non-residential subscribers, as it will cause credit values to vary widely across EDC service territories and between rate-classes, making non-residential customers unviable in some EDC service territories.

selected.title: N.J.A.C. 14:8-9.7(a)
selected.text: Additionally, the commenter notes that most of the EDCs have high demand charges and, therefore, believes it is unlikely that community solar projects will include non-residential “anchor” customers.

selected.title: N.J.A.C. 14:8-9.7(a)
selected.text: The commenter further proposes that the BPU either develop a bill credit based on the Residential Applicable Retail Rate methodology put forward in the commenters’ August 2018 submissions to the BPU, or provide all participating customers a bill credit based on the applicable default residential retail rate schedule.

selected.title: N.J.A.C. 14:8-9.7(a)
selected.text: The commenter’s recommendation is that the BPU implement the second option.

selected.text: (CCSA and Soltage) 187.

selected.text: COMMENT: The commenter encourages the BPU to establish a residential retail rate credit applicable to all residential and non-residential rate classes, believing it to be necessary to support participation in the Pilot Program by all customer classes and, in particular, commercial, industrial, and affordable housing entities that may serve as creditworthy offtakers to support the successful financing of LMI projects.

selected.title: N.J.A.C. 14:8-9.7(a)

question: As a residential consumer in New York, how does the Community Distributed Generation policy enable me to receive credits for renewable energy, and what are the key provisions of this policy?
gold_answers: The policy allows multiple customers to subscribe to and receive credits for the electricity produced from off-site renewable generation facilities, making it possible for renters and low-income residents to receive credits for renewable energy. Key provisions include a minimum of 10 members for community energy projects, a maximum size of 2 MW, and allocation of at least 1 MWh/year to each subscriber.

on the average unit costs of bridges from 2016 through 2020, as submitted by States to the Federal Highway Administration, as required by section 144(b)(5) of title 23, United States Code: Provided further, That for purposes of determining the distribution of funds to States under this paragraph in this Act, the Secretary shall calculate the total deck area of bridges classified as in poor or fair condition based on the National Bridge Inventory as of December 31, 2020: Provided further, That, subject to the following proviso, funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to States shall be used for highway bridge replacement, rehabilitation, preservation, protec tion, or construction projects on public roads: Provided further, That of the funds made available under this paragraph in this Act that are distributed to a State, 15 percent shall be set aside for use on off-system bridges for the same purposes as described in the preceding proviso: selected.text: RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS # A. Low-To-Moderate Income Energy Independence Incentive Program A one-time $\$3,000$ cash incentive (“LMI Incentive) is available to any residential DGIC qualifying as Low-to-Moderate Income who installs an eligible DGF using Renewable Energy.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In order to receive the LMI Incentive, the qualifying Low-to-Moderate Income residential customer shall provide to the Company proof of installation of the Renewable Energy DGF in accordance with the Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection Rule and, prior to receiving the LMI Incentive, must complete a Company-approved Energy Efficiency audit of the customer’s premise.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Additionally, the Renewable Energy DGF installed by the customer must have a nameplate capacity of at least 4 kWDC and shall not be designed to generate more than $110\%$ of the customer’s prior year annual energy usage at that location.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The LMI Incentive shall be available on a first-come, first-served basis and subject to any annual budgetary restrictions described below for calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: No LMI Incentive will be available beyond the end of 2027.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: The Company has discretion to allocate the LMI Incentive budget so that applications and disbursements under this program may be taken and paid throughout the calendar year.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: A Customer shall receive the applicable LMI Incentive amount as a check via U.S. Mail (or electronic payment) following the Company’s inspection and approval of the installation of the Renewable Energy DGF and verification of eligibility.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: In lieu of receiving the LMI Incentive directly, a Customer may assign the LMI Incentive to a solar installer, contractor, or vendor by making such an election in the Customer’s Interconnection Application submitted to the Company.

selected.title: IV. RESIDENTIAL INCENTIVE PROGRAMS
selected.text: Any solar installer, contractor, or vendor assigned the LMI Incentive under this rate shall provide proof of compliance to Company of the following requirements from the Commission’s Mississippi Distributed Generation Rule:

selected.title: § 39-31-10. Offshore wind procurement.

selected.title: § 39-31-10. Offshore wind procurement.
selected.text: The request for proposals shall require all bidders to provide, at a minimum, information on potential environmental impacts through the submittal of an environmental and fisheries mitigation plan, which shall include site and environmental data transparency requirements; a site layout plan and maps that illustrate the location of all onshore and offshore equipment and facilities and clearly delineates the perimeter of the area in which offshore wind turbines will be placed; annualized estimates for all economic benefits, including the specific in-state expenditures and employment proposed during the development, construction, and operation and maintenance phases of the project; a diversity, equity, and inclusion plan that, at a minimum, provides the bidder’s proposed strategy to enable access to employment and vendor opportunities for historically marginalized communities; identification of Rhode Island vendors and other domestic offshore wind supply chain opportunities associated with the project; and a plan outlining the bidder’s intentions with respect to the negotiation of a project labor agreement(s) to cover construction activities on a proposed project.

selected.text: The community solar garden program must be designed to offset the energy use of not less than five subscribers in each community solar garden facility of which no single subscriber has more than a 40 percent interest.

selected.title: 216B.1641 COMMUNITY SOLAR GARDEN.
selected.text: The owner of the community solar garden may be a public utility or any other entity or organization that contracts to sell the output from the community solar garden to the utility under section 216B.164.

selected.title: 216B.1641 COMMUNITY SOLAR GARDEN.
selected.text: There shall be no limitation on the number or cumulative generating capacity of community solar garden facilities other than the limitations imposed under section 216B.164, subdivision 4c, or other limitations provided in law or regulations.
